name: list_source_connectors
description:
Retrieves the Source connectors available to your team, including their identifier, type, name, description, and documentation link. The connectors are ordered by `connector_id`, and then by `type`. The ordering is case-sensitive, so a `connector_id` in uppercase is listed before one in lowercase.

Use the `connector_id` value returned in this response to call the [Get Configuration Details of a Source Connector](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-sources-connectors-connector-id) endpoint and retrieve the configuration settings that the connector accepts. Connectors that your team does not have access to are not listed. A connector in beta is listed only if it has been enabled for your team.

Read [Find your Source Connector](/reference/creating-a-pipeline-with-hevo-api#step-1-find-your-source-connector) for more information about how to find the connector for your Source.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Value used to retrieve the next set of results. Provide the `next_cursor` value returned in the previous API response.
Maximum number of results the API should return. If not set, the API returns up to 100 items.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: (Optional) Filters the response to return only the connectors of the specified Source type. This parameter accepts a single value, and the value is not case-sensitive. A value that does not match any Source type returns an empty `data` array.
parameters.name: type

code.description: Status of the API call. Returns `Success` for a successful request.

data.description: List of Source connectors available to your team.

connector_id.description: Identifier of the connector. A connector that ingests data from several Source types is listed once for each type. Send this value as `source.connector_id` while creating a Pipeline. For example, _SOURCE_CONNECTOR_MYSQL_.

type.description: Source type that the connector ingests data from. Send this value as `source.type` while creating a Pipeline. For example, _AURORA_.

display_name.description: Display name of the Source. For example, _Amazon Aurora MySQL_.

description.description: Short explanation of what the connector ingests, and the Source it ingests from.

documentation_url.description: Link to the documentation for this Source.

in_beta.description: Indicates whether the connector is in beta. A connector in beta is listed only if it has been enabled for your team.

next_cursor.description: Value you can use to fetch the next set of results. Specify this value in the `cursor` query parameter to fetch additional results. This is `null` when no more results are available.

has_more.description: Indicates whether more results are available.
